**Answer.** No. Overlaid on both store photographs (@fig-photo-match), the [target-compliant reconstruction](2026-10-05-01-can-we-reconstruct-the-ft-mighty-mini-explorer-within-tolerance.qmd) reveals clear visual shape mismatches. The real aircraft features rounded, raked wingtips rather than square cuts, an extended curved nose and lower chin rather than a flat slab ending under the canopy, a noticeably shorter and more swept vertical stabilizer, and an empennage boom with less rearward taper. While scalar dimensions and mass properties land within published tolerances, the underlying aerodynamic and structural contours diverge materially from the photographic build.
